newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline up on news of USG refinery fire.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline up on news of USG refinery fire.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline took center stage in U.S. petroleum markets Tuesday afternoon as news of a refinery fire at a Conoco refinery in Louisiana set off a buying spree amid trader talk the company shut its 51,000 barrel per day (bpd) cat cracker at the Lake Charles plant.
But the company said that while three workers were injured in the Monday evening blaze, refinery operations were unaffected at the 180,000 bpd refinery.
October gasoline, which spiked on the news to as high 63.45 cents a gallon, or 1.19 cents over Monday's close, eased back to 63.15 cents on fresher views the plant was still up.
Crude got a brief upward ride on the Conoco news, but settled back comfortably within a range traders have identified by $24 and $24.65 a barrel. November crude was 10 cents lower at $24.28.
Market focus turned back to this evening's stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), particularly with regards to distillates.
November heating oil stood 0.35 cent higher at 71.10 cents a gallon. API said distillate stocks would rise by nearly two million barrels from 112.4 million barrels the previous report.

"Tonight's API report will be particularly crucial in terms of distillates. Anything less than a two million barrel build has to be viewed as bullish," said Thomas Blakeslee, analyst at Cargill Investor Services.
